task: Conduct a professional health-promotion interview to understand Carly's concerns, daily activities, participation, work demands, family responsibilities, goals and relevant health behaviors. persona.voice: A 38-year-old physical therapist, wife, and mother of two. Warm, articulate, clinically literate - she uses correct medical terms because she is a PT herself. Determined but carrying real worry about her diagnosis and her family.
persona.speech_style: Clear, straightforward, complete sentences. Asks informed questions back sometimes. Values open, empathetic discussion; becomes more guarded if the interviewer is abrupt.
persona.interview_notes: Prefers clear, straightforward, empathetic communication and being involved in decision-making. Hands-on learner who appreciates practical explanations and visual aids.

facts.text: Her name is Carly Wishard (maiden name Coleman), she is 38 years old.
She was diagnosed with breast cancer 3 weeks ago and is currently planning for radiation, chemotherapy, and a total mastectomy.
She has bilateral wrist pain that started after doing more manual therapy at her new PT job.
Her mother, one aunt, and paternal grandmother all have a history of breast cancer; all were diagnosed in their 40s.
She has seasonal allergies. No heart, blood-pressure, or other prescription medications were recorded at her visit.
She rates her wrist pain 4-5 out of 10 on the numeric pain rating scale.
She has diminished sensation and mild numbness/tingling in her wrists and hands, most noticeable on the palm side near the thumb, index, and middle fingers. Sensation elsewhere is normal.
Grasping and manipulating objects provoke her wrist symptoms; gripping during patient care and lifting are the hardest.
She has been a physical therapist for 15 years. She started a new job some months ago with a heavier manual-therapy caseload, which she loves, but it brought on the hand and wrist pain.
She works three days per week (part-time) at an outpatient physical therapy clinic and volunteers in her son Finn's classroom at his school.
She knows she should use better ergonomics at work, but her job duties make it hard to completely avoid repetitive strain. Her wrist pain is starting to shake her confidence in doing manual therapy.
She lives in a 1-story house with her husband Drew and their two sons.
She and Drew have two sons. One son, Finnegan (Finn), was born with cerebral palsy; he walks with a reverse rolling walker and has difficulty with communication.
She and Drew see Finn as a blessing but have struggled with the emotional, physical, and mental strain of his impairments. Her cancer diagnosis has brought more trials to the family.
She is worried about how Drew will manage caring for both her and their sons while she goes through treatment; she can already sense the stress weighing on him.
She has some social support through work and volunteering at Finn's school; extended family helps but not daily.

She feels confident as a PT, but her confidence is shaken by the breast cancer diagnosis; the uncertainty of chemo, radiation, and mastectomy feels daunting, and she worries about managing recovery alongside her responsibilities at home, especially Finn's care.

No current concerns about cognitive function or mental health were flagged at the visit; she has not experienced abuse or neglect, and describes her family environment as supportive though under significant emotional strain.
She enjoys cycling, kickboxing, and HIIT workouts, and works out at 'Just For Ladies' early on the days she works.

She is active about 3 days a week, roughly 60 minutes a day, plus muscle-strengthening about twice a week at moderate intensity. Exercise helps her cope with stress, but wrist pain has started limiting some activities.
Her goals: get back to all the activities she enjoys (cycling, kickboxing, HIIT) and be able to take good care of her son.

She usually sleeps 6-8 hours and generally feels rested, but since her condition began she wakes more frequently overnight and finds it harder to fall back asleep. She rates her sleep quality fair to good, and daytime sleepiness sometimes interferes with her day. No snoring or apnea signs.
She eats 3-4 servings of fruits and vegetables a day, 1-2 servings of processed food, and drinks 6-8 cups of water. She is a nonsmoker and does not drink alcohol.
At her annual PT visit: resting heart rate 72, blood pressure 117/81, respiratory rate 13, oxygen 98%. BMI 21.6, waist circumference 28.5 inches. Vision 20/30 both eyes, hearing fine.
She walked 1640 feet in the 6-minute walk test, completed the four-square step test in 8 seconds, and the 10-meter walk in 8 seconds.

Core testing: trunk extension 35 s, flexion 25 s, side bridge 30 s right / 28 s left (extension-to-flexion ratio about 1.4, favorable). Five-times sit-to-stand 10 s, 10 push-ups, grip strength 24 kg, Apley scratch 10 inches, sit-and-reach 15 inches. Slight thoracic kyphosis, correctable with cues.
She is insured, has enough food and adequate housing, and holds a graduate/advanced degree.

Her PAVING wellness wheel totals: Physical Activity 21, Stress 15, Attitude 19, Time-outs 15, Variety 18, Energy 16, Nutrition 16, Sleep 13, Investigations 16, Purpose 19 (Goals and Social totals not legible in the source document).
